scenario: AITA for being uncomfortable when my boyfriend speaks Spanish to his family around me? | I’m very rarely with my boyfriend and his family, but the few times I have been, they’d only communicate with one another through Spanish, which is a language I hardly know at all. His whole family speaks English as well, but they choose to speak Spanish to one another around me, which makes me uncomfortable because a lot of times it’s regarding plans we’ve made and then my boyfriend has to turn to me and translate what they’ve all been saying, and often he leaves things out and forgets to tell me those necessary details until later. Now of course I don’t mind if it’s like, his siblings to his mother in a conversation that shouldn’t involve me, but when they’re talking with my boyfriend as he’s sitting right next to me, I just feel weird. I understand it’s their “normal language” as my boyfriend calls it, and I’m not trying to be all up in the business or try to have them change their ways, it just makes me feel left out and extremely confused and even a little awkward... I’ve mentioned it to him and he gets defensive and angry, like they’re not going to change to make me more comfortable. I just feel that if the roles were reversed, I would have my family speak to me in a language my boyfriend would understand so he wouldn’t feel left out or like he’s missing something important. Before anyone tells me to simply learn Spanish, first of all, it’s not that easy and second, I am learning Spanish...trying to at least... I feel like I AM the asshole but I don’t want to be...so someone just tell me, am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being unreasonable or not in this situation with my boyfriend and his family. Let me start by laying out what's happening. So, I don't get to spend much time with my boyfriend and his family, but when I do, they speak Spanish to each other, even though they all know English. I don't speak much Spanish, so when they're talking in Spanish, especially about plans we've made, it makes me feel left out and confused. My boyfriend has to translate things for me, but he often leaves out details or forgets to tell me important stuff until later. That's frustrating because I feel like I'm missing out on important information. I understand that Spanish is their "normal" language, and I don't want to come off as demanding or trying to change their ways. But when they're talking with my boyfriend while he's sitting right next to me, it just feels weird. I feel excluded and awkward. I've mentioned this to my boyfriend, but he gets defensive and angry, saying they're not going to change to make me more comfortable. That makes me feel like I'm the asshole for even bringing it up. I also thought about if the roles were reversed. Would I have my family speak to me in a language my boyfriend understands so he doesn't feel left out? Probably, yes. So why is it different when it's my boyfriend's family? That makes me question if I'm being unreasonable or if my feelings are valid. I know some people might suggest I just learn Spanish, but it's not that simple. I'm already trying to learn, but it takes time and effort. Plus, I feel like it's not just about the language; it's about feeling included and not left out in family conversations. So, am I being the asshole here? Or are my feelings justified? I need to figure out if my discomfort is reasonable or if I'm overreacting. First, I should consider the cultural context. For many families, speaking their native language is a way of preserving their culture and connecting with each other. It's not necessarily meant to exclude anyone. However, when it comes to involving a partner who doesn't speak the language, it can create feelings of exclusion. I also need to think about communication. My boyfriend gets defensive when I bring this up, which might make me feel like my concerns aren't valid. But it's important to express feelings without feeling guilty. Maybe there's a way to communicate this without making him feel attacked. Another angle is to consider mutual respect. If I were in his position, would I expect his family to speak English around me? Probably, yes, to make me feel included. So, is it fair to expect the same from his family? I also wonder about the practicality of learning Spanish. It's a long process, and in the meantime, I still deserve to feel included in family conversations. So, expecting his family to speak English around me might be a reasonable request, especially when discussing plans that involve me. On the other hand, I don't want to come off as demanding or disrespectful of their culture. It's a delicate balance between wanting to feel included and respecting their traditions. Maybe the solution is to find a middle ground. Perhaps they can speak English when I'm around, or at least include me in the conversation by translating important parts. It's about making me feel valued and included without forcing them to abandon their language entirely. In the end, I think my feelings are valid. Feeling excluded and confused is natural in this situation. It's important to communicate these feelings respectfully and find a compromise that works for everyone. I shouldn't feel like the asshole for wanting to feel included and valued in my boyfriend's family.
